thesis."},{"candidate_id":"c2","keep":false,"stance":"neutral","why":"Mostly navigation text listing document release dates with no substantive information on the policy outlook."},{"candidate_id":"c3","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"The September 2026 statement shows the Committee raised the target range, the opposite of the cut the thesis predicts."},{"candidate_id":"c4","keep":true,"stance":"neutral","why":"July minutes show the Committee held rates steady, which is historical baseline context for judging a later cut."},{"candidate_id":"c5","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Most September participants expected another rate increase, which weakens the case for a cut at the next meeting."},{"candidate_id":"c6","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Sixteen of 18 dot-plot participants anticipated at least one more hike this year, implying a hiking rather than cutting bias."},{"candidate_id":"c7","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Futures pricing shows an 85 percent chance of at least one hike, so market expectations run against a cut."},{"candidate_id":"c8","keep":true,"stance":"neutral","why":"January minutes record a hold decision, which is historical background on how the Committee has been acting."},{"candidate_id":"c9","keep":true,"stance":"supports","why":"Several January participants favored downward adjustments to the target range, a dovish signal that backs the cut link."},{"candidate_id":"c10","keep":true,"stance":"supports","why":"A rising unemployment rate since mid-last-year is a labor-market weakness that could justify easing."},{"candidate_id":"c11","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"The labor market is described as solid and stable, which lowers the need for a rate cut."},{"candidate_id":"c12","keep":true,"stance":"neutral","why":"The CPI release header provides the September 2026 inflation release context and monthly CPI rise needed to judge the policy outlook."},{"candidate_id":"c13","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Headline CPI rose to 3.7 percent year over year, a rising inflation reading that argues against cutting."},{"candidate_id":"c14","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Core CPI rose to 2.6 percent from 2.4 percent, showing underlying inflation accelerating against a cut."},{"candidate_id":"c15","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Energy prices rose 20.4 percent over the year, adding inflation pressure that weakens the case for a cut."},{"candidate_id":"c16","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Waller says policy will focus on the inflation side of the mandate for the near term, which argues against easing."},{"candidate_id":"c17","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Oil supply disruptions from the Middle East conflict add upward inflation pressure, reducing room for cuts."},{"candidate_id":"c18","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Threatened new tariffs could push inflation up again, which argues against a near-term cut."},{"candidate_id":"c19","keep":true,"stance":"contradicts","why":"Strengthening activity and a stated lack of concern about tighter policy point toward holding or hiking rather than cutting."},{"candidate_id":"c20","keep":true,"stance":"neutral","why":"Participants viewing the policy rate as not restrictive is ambiguous for a cut: it could mean room to ease or no need to ease."}]}
